user.title: Host the listener
user.description:
Your sign dials out to Home Assistant; nothing dials the sign. This step binds the port it will call.

Home Assistant looks reachable at **{detected_ip}**. Keep the default port unless you have already changed it on the sign over USB.

data_description.port: 11113 is the firmware default, so a sign that has never been reconfigured needs no port argument at all.
data_description.host: 0.0.0.0 listens on every interface, which is the right default: Home Assistant's own address can change, and a bind to an address that later disappears fails on restart.

instructions.title: Point your sign at Home Assistant
instructions.description:
Your sign **cannot be discovered**, and it cannot be told where to find Home Assistant over the network -- the server address is read-only over the wire. You must set it one of two ways.

**Option A -- USB (always works, needs physical access)**

Connect the sign's micro-USB port to a computer. It appears as a serial port at 115200 8N1 (`/dev/ttyUSB0` on Linux, `/dev/cu.usbserial-*` on macOS). Then:

```
server_tcp_set {detected_ip} {port}
flash_save
cs 3
```

`cs 3` forces a reconnect without a reboot.

**Option B -- DNS (no physical access, but only if the sign already holds a hostname)**

Re-point that hostname at {detected_ip} in your local DNS. The sign connects here on its next attempt.

**Recommended:** use Option A once to set a *hostname you control*, not an IP address. Then you can move Home Assistant, change its address, or switch back to the Visionect server later without ever touching USB again.

Note that pointing a sign here takes it away from the Visionect Software Suite completely: the sign holds exactly one server address and dials exactly one server.

error.port_in_use: Something else already holds that port. Stop it, or pick another port -- but note that only the hostname can be moved in DNS, so changing the port means another USB trip.
error.cannot_bind: Home Assistant could not bind that address on this host.

abort.already_configured: A Visionect listener is already configured. One listener serves every sign.

data_description.persist_params: Issue a flash save after every parameter write. Without it a setting is RAM-only and is lost at the next reboot; with it every change costs a flash write.

no_device_connected.title: No Visionect sign has connected
no_device_connected.description:
Home Assistant is listening on {host}:{port} and has accepted {accepted} connections, but no sign has identified itself.

A sign cannot be discovered: it has to be pointed at this address explicitly, over USB (`server_tcp_set` + `flash_save` + `cs 3`) or by re-pointing a hostname it already holds.

If Home Assistant runs in a container on a bridge network, the port is not reachable from the LAN until you publish it -- and **that needs the container recreated, not restarted**: `docker compose up -d --force-recreate`. A plain `docker restart` will appear to change nothing.

port_in_use.message: Could not bind port {port}: {error}. This is usually transient -- a reload race or a lingering socket -- so Home Assistant will keep retrying.

cannot_bind.message: Cannot bind {host}:{port}: {error}. Waiting will not fix this; change the bind address.

display_image.name: Display image
display_image.description: Show a picture on a sign. Passing an entity id sets a live source that is re-read at every contact; passing a path or URL snapshots it now.

image.name: Image
image.description: An image.* or camera.* entity id, an http(s) URL, or a local file path inside allowlist_external_dirs.

snapshot.name: Snapshot
snapshot.description: Capture an entity once instead of making it a live source.

fit.name: Fit
fit.description: How to place the picture on the panel.

background.name: Background
background.description: Letterbox colour as #RRGGBB. White is the paper colour, so white letterboxing is invisible; black is a solid bar.

dither.name: Dither
dither.description: Bayer is bi-level only, so it is treated as blue noise at 4-bit.

display_text.name: Display text
display_text.description: Render a short message: one font, one size, word-wrapped, vertically centred. For anything more elaborate, serve an HTML page and use a url content source -- that gives you a real layout engine.

size.name: Size
size.description: Font size in pixels on a 1440x2560 canvas.

set_content_source.name: Set content source
set_content_source.description: Say what this sign displays. The source is re-read at the moment the sign is reachable, so an hourly sign shows a fresh render every hour with no automation.

entity_id_source.name: Entity
entity_id_source.description: The image.* or camera.* entity to re-read at every contact.

url.name: URL
url.description: Fetched at push time and rendered as a template first, so ?t={{ now().timestamp() }} works for cache-busting.

headers.name: Headers
headers.description: Outgoing HTTP headers, which is how you authenticate a renderer, e.g. Authorization: Bearer <token>.

clear_content.name: Clear content source
clear_content.description: Forget this sign's content source. The screen keeps whatever it is showing until the next push.

update_now.name: Update now
update_now.description: Re-resolve the content source and push on the next contact.

refresh.name: Refresh display
refresh.description: Re-push the current frame even if the sign reports it is already in sync. Every push to this hardware is full-screen, so this is a genuine full-screen refresh.

ghost_clear.name: Ghost clear
ghost_clear.description: Experimental. Queues an inverse full-screen pass to clear e-ink ghosting. The server-side signalling is verified; the firmware's reaction to it is not, and on a stock configuration it may do nothing beyond a second push.

read_parameters.name: Read device parameters
read_parameters.description: Queue a TCLV read. Reads are nearly free and are coalesced as a set.

ids.name: Parameter ids
ids.description: A list of TCLV ids, e.g. [29].

write_parameters.name: Write device parameters
write_parameters.description: Queue a TCLV write, last-write-wins per id, followed by a read so the device gets the last word. Eight ids -- the hardware id, the server address and the Wi-Fi credentials -- are read-only over the network and can only be set over USB.

values.name: Values
values.description: A mapping of TCLV id to integer, e.g. {"29": 30}.

persist.name: Persist
persist.description: Save to flash afterwards. Overrides the entry option for this call.

list_device_files.name: List device files
list_device_files.description: Read the sign's filesystem root. There is no list opcode in the protocol; this is a read of ".", which is what the vendor's own server does. One round trip, so it answers immediately when the sign is connected and is queued for its next contact otherwise.

read_device_file.name: Read device file
read_device_file.description: Pull one file off the sign's own flash and, if it is a stored frame, decode it into a picture. This is slow: the device answers 1 KiB at a time at about 2.3 KiB/s and offers no seek, so a file takes one to nine minutes and a lost reply restarts it. Note these files are not a live framebuffer -- on this firmware they are Visionect's shipped demo screens and do not change when you push. What the panel is showing is answered for free by the "Display out of sync" sensor.

filename.name: File name
filename.description: A path from the file listing, slash included, such as /image0.pv2.

decode.name: Decode
decode.description: Decode the file as an image into the Device file entity. Turn off to fetch the bytes and only report the headers.

timeout.name: Reply timeout
timeout.description: Seconds to wait for any one 1 KiB reply before treating it as lost.

attempts.name: Attempts
attempts.description: How many times to restart the transfer from the beginning after a lost reply. There is no seek, so there is no way to resume.
